question_text: A 59-year-old woman with a past medical history of atrial fibrillation currently on warfarin presents to the emergency department for acute onset dizziness. She was watching TV in the living room when she suddenly felt the room spin around her as she was getting up to go to the bathroom. She denies any fever, weight loss, chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, lightheadedness, or pain but reports difficulty walking and hiccups. A physical examination is significant for rotary nystagmus and decreased pin prick sensation throughout her left side. A magnetic resonance image (MRI) of the head is obtained and shows ischemic changes of the right lateral medulla. What other symptoms would you expect to find in this patient?
